:::{#exr-wilks-lrt-quadratic}
#### Likelihood ratio statistic for a point null hypothesis

With a scalar parameter $\param$,
the point null hypothesis $H_0: \param = \param_0$
imposes $q = 1$ constraint.
Use @exr-wilks-taylor
to approximate the [likelihood ratio statistic](#def-lrt-stat) $\lrstat$
in terms of the [observed information](#def-oinf) $\oinf(\hthml)$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-wilks-lrt-quadratic}

Under $H_0$, the only allowed value is $\param_0$,
so the restricted MLE is $\hparam_0 = \param_0$.
Substituting the approximation from @exr-wilks-taylor:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lrstat
&= 2\paren{\llik(\hthml) - \llik(\hparam_0)}
&& \text{(definition of $\lrstat$)}\\
&= 2\paren{\llik(\hthml) - \llik(\param_0)}
&& \text{($\hparam_0 = \param_0$)}\\
&\approx 2\paren{\llik(\hthml) - \paren{\llik(\hthml) + \frac{1}{2}\hess(\hthml)(\param_0 - \hthml)^2}}
&& \text{(substitute the expansion)}\\
&= 2\paren{\llik(\hthml) - \llik(\hthml) - \frac{1}{2}\hess(\hthml)(\param_0 - \hthml)^2}
&& \text{(distribute the minus sign)}\\
&= 2\paren{-\frac{1}{2}\hess(\hthml)(\param_0 - \hthml)^2}
&& \text{(cancel $\llik(\hthml)$)}\\
&= -\hess(\hthml)(\param_0 - \hthml)^2
&& \text{(multiply by 2)}\\
&= -\hess(\hthml)(\hthml - \param_0)^2
&& \text{($(a - b)^2 = (b - a)^2$)}\\
&= \oinf(\hthml)(\hthml - \param_0)^2
&& \text{(observed information is the negative Hessian)}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
